chapter: Lucky Millinder and Duke Ellington's band, 1948-52
title: Playing the plunger: Tricky Sam's ya-ya versus Tyree's wa
summary: Jackson copied Tricky Sam's plunger sound, relaxing it, getting closer to the ya-ya than Tyree Glenn.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Growl, plunger and derby: the trumpet mute tradition

blocks.x: So when I joined the band and I started to playing the plunger, all I did was take Tricky Sam's style, actually, and relax it, you know, and try to bring it up to, you know, make it a little, you know, more relaxed.
Except you got closer to the "ya-ya" than anybody did.
Well, that was the sound, that was the sound that you wanted.
I know, but Tyree was in there and he played the plunger his own way which was great and sounded marvelous, but it wasn't a "ya-ya." It was "wa."
Well, I know, I know. Well, you see,
So naturally I'm going to try to duplicate that sound because it was the nearest thing to what I thought Ellington would want.
